q-251795.name: Question 1
q-251795.problem:
Consider two sets of $16$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{16},$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{16}.$ You are given that

$$
\begin{aligned} & {\sum }_{i=1}^{16}{x}_{i}=168, \\  & {\sum }_{i=1}^{16}{y}_{i}=158, \\  & {\sum }_{i=1}^{16}{x}_{i}{y}_{i}=1\,742.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, ${S}_{xy}=$
{{field-1}}.
q-251795.worked_solution:
Given a set of $n$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n},$ the statistic ${S}_{xy}$ be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xy} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}{y}_{i}-\frac{1}{n}({\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i})({\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the given statistics in the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xy} & =1\,742-\frac{1}{16}(168)(158) \\  & =1\,742-1\,659 \\  & =83.\end{aligned}
$$

fields.input_html: 83

q-251806.name: Question 2
q-251806.worked_solution:
Given a set of $n$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n},$ the sum of products of deviations from the means can be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xy} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i}{x}_{i}{y}_{i}-\frac{1}{n}({\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i})({\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i})\end{aligned}
$$

First, we calculate the sum of the ${x}_{i}$ and ${y}_{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} & =16+9+12+10+11+11+6+9=84, \\ {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i} & =10+14+8+10+7+8+2+4=63\end{aligned}
$$

We are given that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{x}_{i}{y}_{i}=695.$

Finally, by substituting in the above formula, we get

$$
{S}_{xy}=695-\frac{1}{8}(84)(63)=695-661.5=33.5.
$$

q-251850.name: Question 3
q-251850.problem:
Consider two sets of $20$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{20},$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{20}.$ You are given that

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xx}=60,\,{S}_{yy}=116,\,{S}_{xy}=100.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, ${\sigma }_{y}^{2}=$
{{field-1}}.
q-251850.worked_solution:
Given a set of $n$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n},$ the variance of ${y}_{i}$ can be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{y}^{2} & =\frac{{S}_{yy}}{n},\end{aligned}
$$

where ${S}_{yy}$ is the sum of squared deviations from the mean for the data ${y}_{i}.$

We are given that ${S}_{yy}=116.$ Substituting the given statistic in the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{y}^{2} & =\frac{116}{20} \\  & =5.8.\end{aligned}
$$
